inSimpleTerms: The main async server bootstrap for the Abuse Enforcement Service (AES) written in Rust. It initializes Axum HTTP/gRPC routes, connects to Strato/Manhattan, sets up rate limiters, and starts safety rule evaluation.
whyThisExists: Engineers required an ultra-low latency, memory-safe enforcement service capable of executing hundreds of safety actions per second without GC pauses.
howItAffectsYourReach: Serves as the execution engine for real-time account suspensions, deboosting labels, NSFW tagging, and search visibility filtering.
theGoldenRule: Operate strictly within platform safety guidelines; once AES triggers an automated enforcement action, reach is curtailed instantaneously.

inSimpleTerms: Declarative policy rules for tweet-level enforcement actions. It maps NSFW media scores, scam URLs, duplicate text replies, and toxicity metrics to tweet downranking or tombstoning.
whyThisExists: Enforces granular tweet-level safety interventions without necessarily suspending the entire author account.
howItAffectsYourReach: Posts flagged by these rules receive visibility filtering labels, removing them from For You timelines and Search top results.
theGoldenRule: Do not include suspicious shortlinks or repetitive text strings that match tweet-level safety enforcement filters.

inSimpleTerms: Declarative policy rule definitions for account-level enforcements. Specifies threshold conditions for spam scores, report ratios, and ban-evasion signals that trigger user suspension or deboosting.
whyThisExists: Provides a transparent, version-controlled policy specification for account remediation that safety operators can audit and update.
howItAffectsYourReach: Matching an account-level enforcement rule applies persistent negative labels (e.g. SPAM_HIGH_RECALL), suppressing all outgoing tweets across all feeds.
theGoldenRule: Protect account reputation by preventing spikes in user blocks and reports that trigger automated account-level safety policies.

inSimpleTerms: Client library for communicating with Action Intake Service (AIS). It dispatches finalized enforcement actions (e.g., label writes, suspensions) to downstream execution backends.
whyThisExists: Centralizes mutation execution through a single audited queue to maintain consistency across all safety subsystems.
howItAffectsYourReach: Executes downstream distribution blocks and label attachments that cut off viral reach in real-time.
theGoldenRule: Treat policy warnings seriously; once AIS receives an enforcement command, reach suppression is immediate and platform-wide.

inSimpleTerms: Manages allowlists and exemption policies for verified partners, official government accounts, and internal test users.
whyThisExists: Guarantees that critical public infrastructure accounts and verified partner organizations are protected from automated false-positive bans.
howItAffectsYourReach: Allowlisted entities bypass automated threshold drops and require manual human review before enforcement.
theGoldenRule: Attaining verified organization or government status provides structural protection against automated algorithmic deboosting.

whyThisExists: Essential operational scaffolding required for running enterprise-grade Rust services under high load and observability requirements.
howItAffectsYourReach: Ensures uninterrupted real-time execution of safety pipelines protecting platform integrity.
theGoldenRule: Operate within standard API client behaviors to avoid tripping operational telemetry alarms.

inSimpleTerms: Defines the enforcement decision model and action specifications. It encodes decisions like Skip, SuspendUser, AddLabelsV2, and DropPost, determining what punitive action to dispatch.
whyThisExists: Decouples rule evaluation logic from physical enforcement mutation calls across backend user/tweet stores.
howItAffectsYourReach: Translates safety rule violations into concrete visibility penalties, search blacklists, and algorithmic distribution blocks.
theGoldenRule: Avoid triggering high-confidence abuse detectors, as Decision::Act immediately applies persistent visibility suppression labels.

inSimpleTerms: In-memory deduplication cache preventing duplicate enforcement actions from firing repeatedly on the same entity within short time windows.
whyThisExists: Eliminates redundant network calls and write amplification against Manhattan and Gizmoduck when multiple events fire for one user.
howItAffectsYourReach: Prevents compounding duplicate penalties from being applied multiple times to the same post in rapid succession.
theGoldenRule: Fix flagged issues promptly, as deduplication windows expire quickly and subsequent scans will re-evaluate content.

inSimpleTerms: Defines domain entity models representing Users, Posts, Spaces, Direct Messages, and Cards within the enforcement system.

howItAffectsYourReach: Standardizes how safety scores map across different post types (text, quote, reply, video) in the distribution funnel.
theGoldenRule: Maintain high content quality across all media formats, as entity-level safety checks evaluate your entire profile.

inSimpleTerms: Extracts and normalizes context facts about users and tweets from upstream request payloads and Strato lookups. It aggregates age, engagement rates, report counts, and previous violations.
whyThisExists: Provides safety rule engines with a unified, strongly typed fact snapshot required to evaluate complex conditional policies.
howItAffectsYourReach: Negative facts (high spam report ratio, high block velocity, low account age) combine to cross abuse thresholds and restrict candidate ranking.
theGoldenRule: Keep negative signals low by producing content that does not induce high block or report rates from users.

inSimpleTerms: Implements sliding-window rate limiting and action throttling for abuse enforcement. It ensures automated actions do not exceed safe velocity thresholds.

inSimpleTerms: Computes Pointwise Mutual Information (PMI) metrics across graph entities. It measures the statistical co-occurrence and affinity between users, hashtags, and interaction patterns.
whyThisExists: PMI isolates true organic topical affinity from random baseline correlation across millions of heterogeneous graph edges.
howItAffectsYourReach: High PMI with reputable topic clusters boosts topical relevance in recommendation hubs; high PMI with spam clusters triggers deboosting.
theGoldenRule: Maintain focused, high-relevance topical engagement within recognized domain communities to establish high positive PMI scores.

inSimpleTerms: Computes the statistical ratio of user spam/abuse reports to favorite engagements for accounts across the interaction graph. It measures how frequently an account's content induces negative reporting.
whyThisExists: Raw report counts penalize large viral accounts unfairly; normalizing reports per favorite provides an accurate signal of actual toxic/spam behavior.
howItAffectsYourReach: If an account's spam reports per favorite exceeds calibrated percentiles (>0.9975), it receives an immediate search top tweet blacklist label.
theGoldenRule: Never buy fake engagement or post misleading rage-bait; high report-to-favorite ratios will trigger automatic Agatha blacklists.

inSimpleTerms: Calculates graph proximity and mutual connection density to previously suspended spam accounts. It detects sybil clusters and bot farms via label propagation across the follow graph.
whyThisExists: Spammers operate in interconnected clusters; propagating suspended labels across graph edges uncovers newly created clone accounts.
howItAffectsYourReach: Scoring high on SpamSuspended graph affinity (>0.98) triggers immediate shadowban labels (e.g. SearchTopTweet blacklist).
theGoldenRule: Do not engage with or follow bot farms and follow-back syndicates; graph proximity to suspended accounts degrades your own account score.

theGoldenRule: Avoid high-cardinality mass interaction patterns that trigger streaming probabilistic rate limiters and spam filters.

howItAffectsYourReach: Ensures uninterrupted rule execution; safety checks cannot be bypassed even during heavy system load or partial network outages.
theGoldenRule: System resilience ensures safety policies are uniformly and strictly enforced across 100% of platform traffic.

inSimpleTerms: Defines the directed graph edge structure connecting source and destination user nodes. It carries interaction weights, damping factors, and relationship types across the follow and engagement graph.
whyThisExists: High-throughput graph traversal requires a lightweight, memory-efficient edge primitive that can be mapped rapidly during distributed PageRank iterations.
howItAffectsYourReach: Edges from suspended, spam, or muted accounts carry zero or negative weight, filtering out fake engagement from inflating your reach.
theGoldenRule: Avoid engagement pods or automated follow loops, as low-trust edges are aggressively pruned and do not transmit ranking authority.

inSimpleTerms: Enforces sanity checks and drift limits when generating new UserCred snapshot builds. It validates distribution statistics, mean mass, and node count deltas before publishing scores to production storage.
whyThisExists: A corrupted graph job or faulty PageRank convergence could wipe out reputations for millions of legitimate accounts, causing catastrophic platform-wide feed degradation.
howItAffectsYourReach: Protects accounts from sudden arbitrary reach collapses caused by batch compute anomalies or pipeline bugs.
theGoldenRule: Trust metrics are mathematically shielded against abrupt pipeline regressions, ensuring stable visibility over long time horizons.

inSimpleTerms: Defines the core UserCredV2 data model and the mathematical score transformation formula. It converts raw GraphJet PageRank graph mass into a calibrated 0-100 credibility score using a logarithmic slope and intercept.
whyThisExists: X needed a normalized, bounded reputation score derived from PageRank mass that downstream safety filters and timeline rankers can consume without dealing with raw floating-point power-law distributions.
howItAffectsYourReach: UserCred score acts as a platform-wide trust multiplier; accounts scoring below calibrated thresholds face aggressive deboosting, search blacklisting, and stringent rate limits, while high-cred users bypass spam heuristics.
theGoldenRule: Build authentic graph connectivity with established, verified accounts rather than farming low-quality mass to steadily raise your UserCred reputation score.

inSimpleTerms: The main Scalding/Spark application entry point for the UserCred v2 batch pipeline. It configures MapReduce/Hadoop graph jobs, loads source interaction dumps, and orchestrates distributed PageRank scoring.
whyThisExists: Orchestrates end-to-end execution of daily/weekly graph reputation calculations across petabyte-scale user interaction datasets.
howItAffectsYourReach: Recalculates global reputation scores in batch; changes in your network credibility are materialized and published to online serving stores when this job runs.
theGoldenRule: Long-term graph building pays compounding dividends as batch scoring jobs periodically refresh and solidify your standing.

inSimpleTerms: Holds configurable hyperparameters for the UserCred algorithm, including convergence epsilon, damping factors, maximum iterations, and storage output paths.
whyThisExists: Allows ML platform engineers to tune graph convergence speed, damping factors, and safeguard tolerances without recompiling pipeline binaries.
howItAffectsYourReach: Governs how fast PageRank mass diffuses across the network and how strongly out-of-network connections influence your score.
theGoldenRule: Graph authority propagation follows strict mathematical damping; steady organic growth across multiple hops yields maximum reach.

inSimpleTerms: Provides serialization, deserialization, and bijection codecs for UserCred data structures. It transforms UserCred objects to and from Thrift, Manhattan key-value bytes, and Memcached formats.
whyThisExists: Real-time timeline ranking requires sub-millisecond retrieval of UserCred scores from Manhattan/Strato KV caches via compact binary formats.
howItAffectsYourReach: Enables Home Mixer and Phoenix rankers to instantly look up author credibility during sub-50ms candidate scoring rounds.
theGoldenRule: Maintain clean account state so your serialized credibility payload is immediately accessible to real-time feed rankers.

inSimpleTerms: Represents the raw PageRank mass and graph weight allocated to an individual user node. It captures both source mass and inbound mass propagated through the follow and interaction graph.
whyThisExists: Calculates PageRank power-law distribution over hundreds of millions of nodes, isolating graph weight calculations from business rule formatting.
howItAffectsYourReach: Higher mass directly scales your calculated UserCred score, elevating your tweets in the Phoenix neural ranker and out-of-network recommendation pools.
theGoldenRule: Earn follows and retweets from high-mass authority nodes in your niche to significantly boost your propagated graph mass.

inSimpleTerms: Encapsulates a user node within the UserCred graph computation pipeline, maintaining state across iterative PageRank passes. It tracks current mass, residual mass, and out-degree connectivity.
whyThisExists: Maintains distributed node state in memory across distributed graph iterations without incurring expensive serialization overhead.
howItAffectsYourReach: Accounts with high out-degree to low-credibility spam nodes bleed mass efficiency, reducing their algorithmic authority.
theGoldenRule: Maintain a healthy follow-to-follower ratio and unfollow inactive or spammy accounts that drain your node reputation.

inSimpleTerms: Applies validation filters to determine whether a user account qualifies for inclusion in the UserCred graph calculation. It filters out deactivated, suspended, or zero-activity accounts before graph processing.
whyThisExists: Prevents millions of zombie, deactivated, and spam accounts from polluting the distributed graph matrix and consuming memory.
howItAffectsYourReach: If your account fails validation criteria (e.g. suspended or marked unverified spam), it is excluded from graph mass propagation, zeroing out credibility.
theGoldenRule: Ensure your account maintains verified email/phone credentials and complies with basic active account requirements to remain in the reputation graph.
